the chalcones and the flavanone isolated from the leaves of S. samarangense are the first compounds to be identified as selective inhibitors of prolyl endopetidase among three different serine proteases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
compounds 3-8, and 10 are potential prolyl endopetidase inhibitors.
the chalcones, 7, 9 and the flavanone, 8 were found to be the most active compounds against prolyl- endopeptidace.
the inhibitory activity of these compounds is related to the presence of a chalcone or a flavanone structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
compounds 3-8, 10 and 13 may serve as lead compounds for the development of new prolyl endopetidase inhibitors.
chalcone derivatives are promising inhibitors of prolyl endopetidase.
the inhibition of prolyl endopetidase by compounds 3-8 may be due to the presence of a hydroxyl group at C-2′ and/or a methoxy group at C-4′ of the flavonoid skeleton.
